verdict.rationale: Docs show sessions are persisted to disk and can be resumed after interruption, and hosting docs describe subprocess supervision, scaling, and multi-tenant isolation for Docker/Kubernetes deployments — a foundation for surviving restarts. However there is no evidence of a native durable-execution model (automatic checkpoint/replay, exactly-once guarantees) or integrations with durable-execution frameworks like Temporal/Restate; resuming appears to be a manual/session-file mechanism rather than a full durable-execution guarantee across deploys. missing for 10: explicit durable-execution framework integrations, automatic crash-recovery/replay guarantees, and independent evidence of long-lived agent survival across real deploys.
